entities.summary: Institut de Radioastronomie Millimetrique (IRAM) is an international research institute and Europe's leading center for radio astronomy at millimeter wavelengths. Its mission is to explore the universe, study its origins and its evolution with two of the most advanced radio facilities in the world:The NOEMA observatory, an array of currently eleven 15-meter antennas located in the French Alps on the Plateau de Bure at more than 2550 meters above sea level. NOEMA is the most powerful millimeter observatory of the Northern Hemisphere. The IRAM 30-meter telescope, located at 2850 meters altitude on Pico Veleta in the Spanish Sierra Nevada.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: IRAM's radio facilities have enabled groundbreaking discoveries in the field of millimeter astronomy, such as the detection of water vapor and dust in distant galaxies. These findings have significantly advanced our understanding of galaxy formation and evolution.
